notes.title: Yellow Trouble - Demo Out Now!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/4337ef785578087739de2289c7233f9fbf75da5a.jpg[/img]

Hello, the demo for my next game Yellow Trouble is out now! The demo has two main modes: Arcade and Quest.

In Arcade Mode, test your shoot'em up skills through the first 2 stages of the game. Learn how to shoot and move in 8 directions with the aim lock. Master how to use the pulse system. And aim for a 1CC (1 credit clear) with a HISCORE for each of the 3 characters on the Steam leaderboards.

In Quest Mode, the goals are different. Level up your character and skill tree to find the FASTEST way to clear this free roaming run and gun style adventure with action RPG elements. Or ignore the speedrun and simply spend time to explore and max out the skill tree to see what benefits the different skills offer.

Both modes support up to 3 players co-op, so try it with some friends locally or via Steam remote play. You can earn credits and unlock Training Mode just like in the main game as well.

The demo may still contain some bugs so please report them on the community hub. As an unknown solo developer, this helps me a lot and I appreciate your participation. If you enjoy the demo, please tell more people about it and wishlist the game. Thank you very much!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3091650/Yellow_Trouble_Demo/

notes.title: Strategy 1: True Pryzm Battles
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/95e73a5fdda3e95713de005c33b37fd35f7fbf18.jpg[/img]

For those who have attempted a True Pryzm run, it is immediately obvious that the enemies are much more difficult and require a different strategy compared to Normal difficulty. While most enemies could be brute forced through with spamming Attack or even using Escape, enemies now hit harder and have new actions. New enemies such as the Drainer type in the screenshot above not only attack but can also absorb precious clarity.

Since starting clarity is significantly lower in True Pryzm, this means that it is almost necessary to do some clarity absorption from enemies during a True Pryzm run, The good news is that almost all enemy types contain more clarity to be absorbed by the player as well. (Hint: The leech type enemies are the best for this because they are weaker and give more opportunities for clarity stealing.) Learning to manipulate the risk probability becomes more crucial. Absorbing some clarity then escaping is also a valid strategy.

Of course, it is important to also find what works for your play style. Some enemies are just not worth fighting in True Pryzm. But since HP resets with every new battle, you can afford to give yourself some room for experimentation and errors. (As a side note, True Pryzm originally featured persistent HP, meaning you have to maintain HP throughout the run, not just for that one battle. But I decided it would make the game too difficult.) Remember: it doesn't matter if you beat or escaped an enemy with 1 HP left, it still counts as a success.

Now go into the True Pryzm and see if you can make it out!

notes.title: Game Details 7: Rank Criteria
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/d00642f9a0cd6d868726de0bad6774ad77088788.jpg[/img]

As you attempt to achieve rank S in either mode, you may be wondering what the requirements for it are. Ending points are rewarded from the following:

[list]
[*]Survivor count: 2 survivors = 10 points, 3 survivors = 20 points
[*]Clear time (game time, not actual real time with fast forward): Under 90 minutes = 20 points, between 90 and 150 minutes = 10 points
[*]Clarity: 1 point for every amount of clarity remaining under 20 or below, 21 points if remnant clarity is above 20
[*]20 points if the relic is found
[*]20 points if the last boss, Dzyll, is defeated, and an additional 10 points if the best ending in True Pryzm is attained
[/list]

The final rank is calculated based on the total points.

Below 20 points: E
20 to under 40 points: D
40 to under 60 points: C
60 to under 80 points: B
80 to 100 points; A
Above 100 points: S

Also, if your ending rank is green in color, it means it is a no continue clear and the time qualifies for the leaderboards. Do note that rank based timings are only counted for B and above. Timings for ALL do not take into account rank, so you can ignore all the above criteria if going for pure speed. Good luck!

notes.title: Game Details 6: Overcoming Randomness
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/a05d8f7f6a29bf4aca7f1767598748fe5d367ee4.jpg[/img]

Randomness is a challenge facing all who are trapped in the Pryzm. It is the result of the entity Dzyll altering space and time. But it did not count on some humans to have the ability to circumvent it. it is why events can be redone (at the cost of clarity) once it has been observed.

This doesn't apply to just finding items. It also applies to the probability of avoiding enemies. For example, in Richard's A scenario, he is often attacked by a tainted even if he attempts to avoid it. By redoing the same scenario, his chance of avoiding increases until it eventually becomes guaranteed. This works for many other such events.

However, one major factor that shapes the Pryzm happens at the very beginning of the story, the first act to be exact, the one that many players tend to skip through. Depending on the choice on the first night as seen above, players can lock in some parameters in advance. For example, many have discovered that [spoiler]talking to Lindsay grants an increase in starting clarity[/spoiler].

But choosing the others have their advantages too. Talking to Greg and Ann [spoiler]will ensure Ann always finds the locket in her A scenario IF the locket is located in the forest, while Greg is always guaranteed to avoid the various tainted in his D scenario[/spoiler].

And talking to Richard [spoiler]ensures he always avoids enemies in his A scenario, finds the hidden basement in his B scenario, while Sara will always make it to the altar in her C scenario[/spoiler]. What Kyle does the following morning also impacts later parts of the story...

Each of these boosts have their specific advantages and will significantly improve a run if those are your goals. Use this knowledge to plan your next run and make it out with a better time and rank!

notes.title: Game Details 5: Items Found and Clarity
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/f6975f8d0759193d1d36f2510662c655205891b5.jpg[/img]

Anyone who has played Pryzm will know how precious clarity is. It usually only keeps depleting. However, there are various items scattered around the world, such as the voice recorder above. When found, it INCREASES clarity by 20. The challenge is that the location of such items is changed with every New Game.

You can certainly attempt to find them by revisiting stages, but each visit costs more and more clarity. So there needs to be a decision whether you want to search for them as part of your strategy or to head straight for the end goal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/7bc8b0fe491bfc5058a8b82de454f4416f504c8f.jpg[/img]
There are some items that remain in the same area, such as the diary above. Spoiler hint:[spoiler]The key to the door it is located behind is in the very same house, so you only need to redo that scene once if you didn't find it the first time. Definitely worth the clarity spent, even with a pesky enemy encounter.[/spoiler]

Be warned. There are some items and paths that DECREASE clarity. Not everything is worth picking up when making a run (unless you want to unlock a specific path, discover lore, or get item achievements). If you know something reduces clarity, don't pick it up again! But you will NEED certain key items to get the best ending in True Pryzm...

notes.title: Game Details 4: True Pryzm Mode
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/12e31dca0d51a61493afe630c634df8fae0394a0.jpg[/img]

Players who have beaten the game with a rank of B and above will notice that True Pryzm mode becomes unlocked next to New Game. What does this mode do? In short, Normal (New Game) mode was merely the tutorial to get you familiarized with the game mechanics and True Pryzm is the REAL difficulty of the game.

Changes in this mode include:
[list]
[*]Lower starting clarity
[*]Aggressive enemies that deal more damage
[*]New enemy types
[*]Hints that show new paths are all turned off
[*]Certain enemies carry more innate clarity to absorb
[*]New areas that expand the lore and can lead to the true ending (hint is in the image)
[/list]
True Pryzm will test all that you've learnt from Normal mode and challenge the strategy that you will follow. There is more than one way to make it out and it is dependent on what you are trying to achieve. Are you merely trying to escape? Are you trying to save specific survivors? Are you aiming for the fastest completion time? Or are you going for the best rank of S? Whatever it is, give this mode a try when you're ready. Normal and True Pryzm have their own leaderboards. Can you get the best times in both?

Note: Continue+ works for True Pryzm as well, but there is only one Continue+ active at any time. So starting a New Game in Normal will wipe the one for True Pryzm and vice versa.

notes.title: Autoscroll Fast Forward Feature Added
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/9720b3416f752918aa0d9d56dba043f56554945d.jpg[/img]

A new Autoscroll Fast Forward feature has been added in version 1.1.4!

This makes the game fast forward during the text adventure sections when autoscroll is activated. It should make replays much quicker. It is deactivated during combat, the main character selection screen, and within the options menu.

Do note that this will speed through text and events that you may not have seen before. Use it at your own discretion! It also does not make speedrun timings faster as it also speeds up the internal game clock, so it still qualifies for the leaderboards. Lastly, fast forward only works within each game mode that has been completed at least once.

Please give it a try and let me know if it breaks the game in any way. Thank you and keep escaping the Pryzm (at a faster rate)!

notes.title: Game Details 3: Continue+ Mode
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/c173c09027f9a03cf0fedaf1a3cae782a0a568ce.jpg[/img]

Have you survived the Przym or are you still trapped in it? Either way, you may have been wondering what the Continue+ option does.

Every new game changes certain parameters that requires a slightly different escape strategy. The overall story is generally the same, but how you survive it varies, especially if aiming for a good rank or specific achievements. Pryzm offers players some help if they find it too difficult. This is where Continue+ comes in.

[h3]For those wondering how saving works, this game will always auto-save at the start of every area or scene so players do not have to complete a run in one sitting. Simply quit the game and pick up where you left off.[/h3]

Continue+ mode only appears just after you complete an entire game or get a game over, replacing the regular Continue auto-save file. Selecting it puts you back into the game at the start of the second act while retaining every parameter from the previous game. So if you discovered a path that gave you a bonus item or a quicker way to avoid enemies previously, those paths are still the same in Continue+! This will allow you to better plan how to make it to the ending and possibly achieve a better rank. Hindsight is indeed 20/20. And you get an increase in starting clarity too, effectively making every Continue+ easier and easier.

Do note that any form of continuing disqualifies the run from the online leaderboard, but qualifies for all achievements not requiring a 1CC. Also, starting a New Game will make this option disappear. Why would you do this instead of using Continue+? Because many of the parameters of the game are actually set by your choices in the first act, so you may want to start a new game to re-arrange the parameters based on your goals.

notes.title: Game Details 2: Turn-Based Combat
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/7e3bb3a39d3456c9bd198e34d3836cf6decc3a56.jpg[/img]

Players who have played the demo will encounter one turn-based combat situation. This game was designed to be easy to learn so beginners and even non-gamers can get into it fairly quickly. But underneath that simplicity lies a more complex system for those who choose to exploit it.

Watch a video tutorial or read on for a more detailed explanation.

[previewyoutube=SFkd9Xa2axE;full][/previewyoutube]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/59cf031d9387e16e23a613224e6878e4749835cd.png[/img]

The screenshot above shows the standard combat scene. Turn-based combat is just that, players and enemies take turns to execute moves. The numbers above the player's avatar represent the status of the player. At this moment, it is the player's turn and there are 4 options available.
[list]
[*]Attack makes an attempt to attack. It may be ineffective due to bad luck or if the enemy is fast.
[*]Evade makes an attempt to dodge the enemy's next move. It has a high chance of dodging but can sometimes fail.
[*]Clarity opens up the clarity sub-menu.
[*]Risk opens up the risk sub-menu.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/445c9b70ff6b773e6848729f64a17ba06a5943cd.png[/img]

The menu above is the Clarity sub-menu. These are moves that boost the player in some way. Using them cost clarity, represented by C in the player stats.
[list]
[*]ATK Up boosts attack damage for a short period of time and costs 1 clarity point.
[*]DEF Up boosts defense and reduces physical damage taken for a short period of time and costs 1 clarity point.
[*]Heal restores a variable amount of the player's Hit Points/HP for 2 clarity points. If HP drops to 0, the player loses the encounter. But you can retry the stage as long as there is still clarity left.
[/list]
[h3]Clarity is the main resource for the entire game. If it reaches 0, it is a game over![/h3]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/623b66c4af60860bcdfa778486320a1fe6ab23a8.png[/img]

The menu above is the Risk sub-menu and where the combat can get complex. [i]Pryzm[/i] uses a risk system that slightly changes how turn-based combat functions traditionally.
[list]
[*]Crit ATK makes an attempt to perform a critical attack that does triple the normal attack damage and can be stacked with ATK Up.
[*]Escape makes an attempt to flee the encounter. This option is not available in some situations where an enemy has trapped a player.
[*]Absorb makes an attempt to absorb clarity from the enemy. Some enemies contain more clarity than others but the quantity per enemy is finite. There are also other ways to obtain clarity outside of combat.
[/list]
[b]Attempting any Risk move will check the probability of success represented by R in the player stats.[/b] This percentage changes and is determined by the different normal moves performed. In general:
[list]
[*]Normal attacks raise R% by a small variable amount.
[*]Evading raises R% by a large variable amount.
[*]Getting hit by the enemy decreases R% by a small variable amount.
[/list]
The higher the R%, the greater the chance a risk move will be successful. So what is stopping a player from just maximizing the R% by spamming evade? Well, there's a catch. If your R% is more than 100%, it resets to 0. This means that it is almost impossible to get a 100% success rate, which is why these are risky moves! A failed risk move will result in the enemy performing a critical attack or clarity drain on the player. The system, therefore, gives you control of these moves depending on how risk averse you are and how you strategically manipulate the R%.

It is entirely possible to not use any risk move, but you will find it harder and harder to avoid it as your clarity goes down throughout the story. Remember, this game does contain elements from the horror genre so you are not expected to defeat every enemy. Escaping is a very viable option to conserve clarity. But then you would possibly miss out on some key items dropped by enemies... It's decisions like these that define your game run.

Hopefully, this has shown you what you could do with the combat. Now get back into the Pryzm and make it out with the best outcome! (You can apply this knowledge for the demo encounter as well!)

notes.title: Game Details 1: What Is Pryzm?
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/b1fed7823e1e3a0bbebe4f2268d951d33c3af7be.jpg[/img]

Now that I am more familiar with how the Steam backend works after releasing [i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2262880/Heli-Cats/]Heli-Cats[/url][/i], I can finally bring [i]Pryzm[/i] to the platform and utilize the various functions that allow me to realize the game's full potential.

[i]Pryzm[/i] started out as an experimental browser game. Coming from a comics background, the adventure / visual novel genre is the most appropriate continuation for my kinds of stories. However, I am an arcade gamer at heart and such games run counter to the length of what is considered a "full" visual novel (which are usually overly long to the point of being superfluously written to reach a large word count). [i]Pryzm[/i] is my attempt at condensing a full story-based game down to an arcade-like experience.

[h3]In essence, this is an adventure game that can be completed in a relatively short amount of time, but can be replayed over and over to get a better result, namely a better time and end rank.[/h3]
The preferable way to play is to perform a 1CC (one credit clear) like an arcade game. Every new run will randomize key parameters that will require the player to prioritize and adjust their escape strategy based on their goals. With enough runs, players should figure out the most optimal ways to get the best timings.

Players can also take their time with the story if they have no interest in getting the fastest clear times. The game has an auto-save that allows breaks in between. However, do note that there is only ONE auto-save, so save scumming has no benefit except to drain resources, and continuing disqualifies the run from the online leaderboards.

Thrown into the mix is an easy to learn turn-based combat system that hinges on a risk and reward system. Fight or flight becomes an important element that can result in crucial conservation or boosting of resources, or completely mess up a good run. Being arcade-like, game overs are always round the corner, so players must always weigh their decisions to avoid unrecoverable mistakes.

[h3]The Steam version of this game will feature many new upgrades to the original version such as new animations, revamped systems, expanded story elements, configurable controller support, achievements that guide players to learn the lore, and online speedrun leaderboards![/h3]

If any of the above interests you, please wishlist the game. More details will be posted in the future to help players understand the mechanics and special features. Thank you for considering my very non-mainstream / niche games!
